title: ArborMed SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
topics: SOC 2 Type II reports and scope
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture with ArborMed security stakeholders. Discussed report access, control mappings, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS encryption, data residency, and options for Dedicated/Private deployments. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 report and Trust Center link, provide controls mapping spreadsheet, schedule technical deep dive and pilot for encryption/KMS verification.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-14 11:00AM PT | Duration: 50m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (CISO - ArborMed), Daniel Ruiz (Head Infra), Priya Rao (Security Engineer)

00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this focused on SOC two and ISO posture and then Samir can jump into the technical bits, uh hi Maya hi Daniel.
00:12 Maya Thompson: Hi Lena thanks, appreciate it. We're looking to finalize our vendor security review by end of month so want to validate Redwood's artifacts and how they map to our control set.
00:22 Lena Park: Totally, the plan for today is quick overview of the reports we have, trust center access, then Samir will go over RBAC/SSO, logging, and encryption/KMS. We'll capture next steps.
00:34 Samir Patel: Quick note — Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II for the last 12 months, and we maintain an ISO 27001 cert. We also publish our control mappings in the trust center, and we can share the full report under NDA.
00:48 Maya Thompson: Great, scope question — does SOC2 cover Dedicated and Private deployments or only the hosted API?
00:55 Jordan Lee: Good question, some of the controls are platform-wide but there are architecture differences. Our SOC 2 covers our control plane and hosted infra; for Dedicated/Private we map controls and provide additional artifacts — we document that in the trust center and in the controls mapping spreadsheet.
01:12 Daniel Ruiz: So we need the mapping for customer-managed VPC and on-prem options, specifically encryption key management and audit log forwarding.
01:22 Samir Patel: Yes we have a controls matrix that calls out which controls apply and where customers are responsible. For KMS, for the hosted offering we manage encryption at rest with customer-data separation, and we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private via KMS/HSM integrations.
01:40 Priya Rao: Can you clarify the KMS flow — do you hold private keys, or do customers hold them? We need proof that private keys aren't accessible to Redwood ops.
01:50 Samir Patel: For customer-managed KMS it's customer keys in their cloud KMS. For Redwood Dedicated we offer an option to bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) where we don't have plaintext access. For hosted API we use envelope encryption and our KMS is in a restricted tenant; we can provide the HSM and key separation docs. We'll add the diagram to the trust center.
02:10 Maya Thompson: Audit logs — retention and format? We need syslog or S3 export for our SIEM with at least 365 days retention and immutability options.
02:21 Jordan Lee: We export audit trails to an immutable storage backend; retention is configurable. For enterprise customers we can stream logs to customer S3 or SIEM via secure forwarders, and we support GDPR and residency controls. We'll attach an example schema.
02:38 Daniel Ruiz: Is there an API or push mechanism for logs and can we get event-level details (user, action, resource, request id)?
02:45 Samir Patel: Yes we maintain event-level logs with request IDs and actor details. The log schema includes timestamp, principal, action, resource path, ip, request id, status, and additional metadata — we can share the export sample.
03:00 Maya Thompson: About SSO and RBAC — we use SAML via Okta. We need SCIM provisioning and role mappings, plus audit of privileged actions.
03:12 Lena Park: Redwood supports SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is fine-grained — you can map Okta groups to product roles (admin, deployer, reader). Privileged actions are logged and surfaced in the audit log UI and exported.
03:32 Priya Rao: Any separation of duties controls? We need to ensure operators can't approve their own changes to rollout policies or production model changes.
03:40 Samir Patel: We have approval workflows and role constraints in the console; operators need distinct roles for deploy approvals. For Dedicated customers we can enable stricter RBAC and manual approval gates. We'll note that in the controls matrix.
03:55 Maya Thompson: For report access, do we have to sign an NDA? How quickly can you provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO cert?
04:02 Jordan Lee: Typically we provide the SOC 2 under NDA, and the ISO cert publicly in the trust center. We can share both by EOD two days if you sign the NDA — Lena will send the standard doc.
04:18 Daniel Ruiz: Pen testing and vulnerability management — frequency and disclosure process?
04:25 Samir Patel: We run quarterly external pentests and continuous vuln scanning; we publish summary findings and remediation SLAs in the trust center. For enterprise customers we can share the full test report under NDA and coordinate rescan windows.
04:40 Maya Thompson: Data residency — we need US-only data for PHI adjacency. Do you support region pinning and dedicated regions for storage?
04:48 Lena Park: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning for storage and model routing. For Private deployments you can keep everything in your VPC and on-prem. We'll call out the locations in the controls mapping.
05:00 Priya Rao: Any evidence of SOC 2 control testing on encryption key management and logging control?
05:06 Jordan Lee: The SOC 2 report includes cover tests for key management and logging. We'll point to specific section IDs in the report when we share.
05:15 Maya Thompson: Ok, for acceptance criteria we'll need: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, Trust Center access, completed controls mapping, ability to forward logs to our SIEM for 365 days, and KMS BYOK verification.
05:32 Lena Park: That's perfect — we'll aim to deliver the artifacts. Samir, can you lead the KMS verification deep dive with Daniel and Priya?
05:40 Samir Patel: Absolutely, happy to. We can do a 60-minute technical session to walk through key flows and a short test harness for BYOK.
05:50 Daniel Ruiz: Prefer next week Tuesday or Wednesday morning our side.
05:54 Samir Patel: I'll propose Tuesday 10am PT in the follow-up.
06:00 Jordan Lee: I'll invite for the trust center and attach the SOC 2 NDA. Lena will follow up on pricing for Dedicated.
06:08 Maya Thompson: One more question — do you have a controls mapping template we can populate?
06:13 Samir Patel: Yes, Samir: I'll send the template, it's a spreadsheet with column for ArborMed control id, Redwood control reference, evidence link, status, and comments.
06:26 Priya Rao: Great — we'll start mapping and come back with gaps.
06:32 Lena Park: Thanks everyone, recap in chat: Lena send SOC2/ISO, Jordan send Trust Center invite, Samir send mapping and schedule KMS deep dive, customer to fill mapping and share retention details.
06:45 Maya Thompson: Thanks, we'll look for the items and target to complete mapping by the 19th.
06:50 Meeting end.
